_: Controls under 44x44 INSIDE each sheet, MEASURED. Same ratchet as touch-targets.baseline.json: a number may only go DOWN, and the audit fails if one climbs or if one falls without this file being tightened.
_why: touch-targets.mjs loads the 21 screens and measures what is ON them. Nothing inside a sheet, dialog or bottom sheet had ever been measured — New Sale, the product picker, the GRN dialog, Edit SKU, every confirm. That is where money is entered, and it is why a 36px Pack/Carton pill sat in front of Ali on the day he was told every control was 44px.
_first_run: MEASURED on 2026-09-02 by CI, except sale-product-picker which could not be opened on the first two runs and is still loose. What the first real measurement found, inside sheets no audit had ever looked at: New Sale's close button at 17x28, and TWENTY controls in New SKU at 16px tall — the category chips. None of it was reachable by the screen sweep, because none of it is on a screen.
_not_covered: The plain product step — a diaper's pack/carton pills, the screen in Ali's screenshot — is NOT measured. Three CI rounds were spent guessing at the selector that reaches it and none worked; the mixed-carton sheet is driven instead because two existing audits prove that flow. Saying so is the point: an audit that quietly covers less than its name suggests is how 'every control is 44px' came to be said about an app where a 36px pill sat on this very screen. Opener failures now print what was on screen, so the next attempt has evidence.
